narrative: New England beat PIT 20-3. The offense posted -0.07 EPA/play (41% success rate) while the defense allowed -0.36 EPA/play. Turnover margin was 0.

good: Patriots defense was dominant in man coverage against Pittsburgh's offense, forcing the Steelers into complete offensive futility.
R.Stevenson's complementary football and the team's red zone efficiency on defense (held Pittsburgh to 0/1) kept the game firmly in control.
bad: Third down offense remains a problem at 4/12—the team converted at 33%, while Pittsburgh held to 16% conversion rate suggests New England's drive sustainability is still a work in progress.
Red zone offense sputtered at 1/3, meaning the Patriots left points on the field despite a dominant defensive performance.
ugly: Mike Onwenu's broken right ankle is a significant loss on the offensive line heading forward.

playerOfTheGame.reason: Led the team with +3% win probability added.

fanTake: Well, that's more like it. The Patriots defense absolutely suffocated the Steelers in man coverage, holding Pittsburgh to just 3 points in what amounted to a near-total home dominance at Gillette, and TreVeyon Henderson punched in a touchdown to lead a 20-3 victory that felt considerably more convincing than the offensive EPA numbers (-0.07) might suggest. Drake Maye's film showed the kinds of decisions we'll be dissecting all season—the young quarterback is learning on the job against elite defenses—but here's the thing: when your defense is that stout and your complementary football is clicking, you don't need to be brilliant offensively. R.Stevenson earned player of the game honors with 3% win probability added, a reflection of the kind of steady, thankless work that wins football games. The Patriots are now 600 wins deep in franchise history, and while the offensive rhythm from last season's Super Bowl run remains elusive, this is the kind of grinding, defense-first win that could matter come January.
